name: audio-waveform
title: Audio waveform
description: A waveform drawn from peak values with a played portion and click-to-seek, as two SVG paths, light enough to repeat fifty times in a list.
docs: peaks is a list of numbers from 0 to 1 in time order, as many as you have: the bars are resampled to the width, so one set of peaks fits a list row and a full-width player. progress is how much has played, 0 to 1. barWidth, gap and height are in px. It draws two SVG paths however many bars there are, so fifty in a list is fine. The width is only known in the browser, so on the server a flat dotted line stands in until it has been measured. With interactive it is a slider: a press or drag calls onSeek with a position from 0 to 1, the arrow keys seek 5 seconds (2 percent without a duration), Shift three times that, Home, End and the Page keys jump, and a marker shows where a press will land, with the time when duration is known. A screen reader hears '1 minute 23 seconds of 4 minutes 56 seconds', or '42 percent' without a duration. A still waveform is hidden from assistive technology unless you pass a label. Get peaks from your server, or in the browser with peaksFromArrayBuffer(await (await fetch(url)).arrayBuffer()), peaksFromAudioBuffer(buffer) or peaksFromChannelData(samples, count), all from @rhs-ui/primitives/audio-waveform/peaks; for a long file work them out once on the server.
